searchText: do we have 2 working ELs on top of glamsterdam-devnet-5 specs? ethrex and nethermind afaik for focil? <@1386598056320831509> you promised me a censoring builder, is it ready? (no pressure 😁 ) nope 😛 been getting a lot of pressure to do this hahaha i m gonna prioritise this, was spending a lot of time implementing the builder-api in buildoor and testing it with a prototype of prysm. https://github.com/ethpandaops/buildoor/pull/81 think its in a good shape now how can i run a local devnet with ILs? thats probably the best start for me. is there a KT config? nobody cares, this is the focil channel 😁 fair fair 🤣 can you give me a FOCIL kt config? i ll pick up from there unsure, i thought the question was about glam-5, on ethrex we got a focil branch and our focil branch should be up to date with glam-4 and since there are no changes for EL also glam-5 so you support both target gas limit and ILs of fcu? let me quickly reverify but should be yes https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1210529202458071050/1504705932389646336 probably fine, just remove teku, I suppose no client other than ldoestar is rebased on glam-devnet-5 specs yet actually i checked and we dont have target gas limit on fcuv5 only fcuv4, i guess thats a gap to fix will look at it now running a focil devnet with only lodestar with besu and another one with ethrex. I am seeing a lot of missing payloads? pushed a `focil` image with the target gas limit fix on fcuv5 https://github.com/ethpandaops/eth-client-docker-image-builder/actions/runs/26949261364 I filled the FOCIL execution-spec tests after merging them locally with the bal-devnet-7 test release, and ran them using an in-process engine-API fixture runner we have (extended to handle inclusion list payloads and the INCLUSION_LIST_UNSATISFIED status) and got all 13 cases passing I'm unsure if there are other more up to date tests that fit glam-5 Currently there are no more tests but the upcoming spec changes will change existing tests and add new tests. Once the spec changes are figured out, I can discuss with <@510888004366368794> to apply those changes to tests.
